repository_verification.verified_files_sha256_note: Digests as reviewed at repository.commit. Frozen evidence: do not rewrite them to make a suite green. A file that has knowingly moved since review belongs in accepted_drift_sha256 with a reason.

Written/ViewModels/DistillViewModel.swif.reason: A cancelled OAuth sign-in returns the source to .idle rather than .failed, for Spotify, YouTube and Google Calendar alike. Dismissing the sheet is a decision, not a failure, and the second-order effect was worse: failureMessage(for:) returns the first failed source in a modality, so backing out of Spotify made the whole Music card report a failure while Apple Music had just distilled 1,225 rows. Also carries the per-source dual-write gate.

Written/Services/Ontology.swift.reason: A classical recording now yields two terms rather than one: the stamped subject (the composer) and the primary performer, which previously vanished from the Memories card entirely. Term gained `sources`, filled at the five construction sites and unioned on merge, so a chip can say which services back it; the set is built from MusicHighlights.allSongRows rather than the deduplicated set, because dedupe drops the losing row and a term built from survivors would claim one source for a recording present on two. Ontology.subjects is deliberately unchanged — it feeds the discovery card, which other people read, and 0038 exists because performer credits made bad public copy.

Written/Services/SyncService.swift.reason: Header comment corrected, no behaviour change. It claimed `push(source:records:)` refuses health outright; localOnlySources is empty and it does no such thing. The real defect was worse and is already fixed: DistillViewModel.sync never called push for health at all, so distilled_records held zero rows with source='health' for every account that had ever connected it. This is the codebase's own recurring defect — a doc comment describing the opposite of the code — removed at the source rather than left to mislead the next reader.

reference_migrations_note: Historical record of the standalone reference chain. Those files are deliberately NOT vendored into the Written repository: their adapted forms are application_migrations 42-47, and keeping both would be two divergent copies of the same DDL.
application_migrations_reserved_note: 50-54 are the KMS key registry, its vocabulary alignment, the ingestion identity, the wrapped-key binding, and the ordering that stops a pure-duplicate batch recording a key. 55 (server projections) is due in phase server_owned_discovery_and_profiles and 56 (cutover) in legacy_semantic_retirement. The pair has shifted six times; the contract forbids reusing a number, not skipping one, so read a number in WRITTEN_REPOSITORY_INTEGRATION.md as the `role` below rather than as a filename. 56 is irreversible and must not exist on disk before a minimum supported client version does.
